Nhóm hướng tới nghiên cứu và phát triển giải pháp công nghệ cho thử thách "Trò chơi thiết kế nhiệm vụ không gian". Với định hướng ứng dụng Trí tuệ nhân tạo (AI/ML), Khoa học dữ liệu và mô phỏng trực quan, đội mong muốn kết nối các bạn trẻ có cùng niềm đam mê nghiên cứu khoa học vũ trụ và công nghệ số.
summary:
MissionWright is an interactive space mission design and simulation game that allows players to experience the challenges of planning and executing interplanetary exploration missions. Players take on the role of mission engineers, designing spacecraft by selecting components, scientific instruments, launch vehicles, propulsion systems, communication equipment, and power resources while balancing engineering constraints, scientific objectives, and mission budgets.

The game features three exploration campaigns: the Moon, Mars, and asteroid Vesta. Across a seven-stage mission workflow, players plan spacecraft configurations, evaluate orbital and resource requirements, launch their vehicles through 3D simulations, respond to unexpected mission events, and operate planetary rovers to complete surface exploration objectives.

By combining engineering decision-making, scientific exploration, resource management, and interactive 3D simulations, MissionForge makes complex space mission concepts more accessible and engaging. It addresses the challenge by turning space mission design into a hands-on learning experience where players can understand the trade-offs, risks, and teamwork involved in real-world space exploration.
details:
MissionWright is an interactive 3D space mission design and simulation game developed to make space exploration and spacecraft engineering more accessible and engaging. The project allows players to experience the role of a space mission engineer by designing spacecraft, planning exploration missions, managing limited resources, and making critical decisions throughout a simulated space journey. Players can choose between three destinations: the Moon, Mars, and the asteroid Vesta, each presenting different levels of difficulty, mission requirements, and planetary exploration challenges.

The game follows a seven-step mission workflow, beginning with spacecraft design and engineering. Players select and configure different spacecraft components, including propulsion systems, power sources, communication equipment, scientific instruments, and other essential subsystems. The system then evaluates their designs based on engineering parameters such as spacecraft mass, launch capacity, available delta-v, power generation and consumption, communication performance, and mission budget. Once the design is completed, players proceed to the launch and flight simulation stages, where they experience the challenges of launching a spacecraft, navigating its journey, managing mission resources, and responding to unexpected events. If the spacecraft successfully reaches its destination, players can continue to the planetary surface exploration stage, where they operate a rover and complete scientific objectives specific to the selected destination.

MissionWright provides an interactive learning environment where users can understand how different engineering decisions influence the success or failure of a space mission. Instead of learning isolated concepts from textbooks, players can experiment with spacecraft configurations, compare design alternatives, and observe the consequences of their decisions. The project aims to promote STEM education, develop engineering problem-solving and systems-thinking skills, and inspire greater interest in space science, planetary exploration, and aerospace technology.

The project was developed primarily using HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript with ES modules. Three.js and WebGL were used to create interactive 3D environments, spacecraft visualizations, planetary maps, launch sequences, and surface exploration experiences. The game also uses procedural generation techniques to create 3D objects, terrain, and visual effects through code. Custom mathematical models support spacecraft engineering calculations, resource evaluation, and mission simulations, while browser LocalStorage is used to preserve player configurations and mission progress. The application is designed to run directly in a modern web browser without requiring specialized hardware.

What makes MissionWright creative is its combination of spacecraft engineering, mission planning, resource management, interactive flight simulation, and planetary rover exploration within a single continuous experience. Rather than presenting space exploration as a passive learning topic, the project turns it into a series of engineering challenges in which players must make meaningful decisions and balance competing requirements. During development, particular attention was given to scientific relevance, engineering constraints, educational accessibility, mission diversity, and browser performance. The three destinations provide different exploration scenarios, while the increasing difficulty encourages players to improve their spacecraft designs and strategic thinking.

Ultimately, MissionWright aims to bridge the gap between theoretical knowledge and practical understanding of space exploration. By allowing users to design, simulate, and operate their own space missions, the project encourages curiosity, creativity, and a deeper appreciation of the engineering challenges involved in exploring our Solar System.
